title: Finish protecting a framed picture for a move: push foam corner protectors onto its two bare corners
instruction: Fit the two loose foam corner protectors onto the picture frame's two bare corners, then let go of them.
context: Movers and hand packers push snug foam corner protectors onto framed pictures, mirrors, glass panels and furniture before wrapping them, so a knock in transit doesn't split a mitre or crack the glass (O*NET 53-7062, 53-7064). Each protector grips by squeezing, so it must be lined up level with the frame's edge and pushed fully home along both edges at once, without shoving the loose frame off its supports.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. (1) Two padded blocks, fixed: pine 2x4 offcuts covered in grey carpet, 16 long (x), 8.9 wide and 3.8 tall, centred at x 30, y +18.5 and -18.5. (2) A picture frame lying face down on the blocks, 1.1 kg: oak moulding 3 wide and 2.5 thick, 30 front to back (x) by 40 across (y), centred at x 30, y 0; glass, mount and hardboard back fill its opening (from 4 mm behind its front to 5 mm short of its back). The blocks are under its two 30 cm sides, so each corner sticks out 7 past the blocks' ends. Its corners are at x 15 and 45, y +20 and -20. (3) Four white cross-linked polyethylene foam corner protectors, 20 g each: a block 7 x 7 and 4.5 tall with an L-shaped pocket cut into two adjacent sides, 4.5 deep each way and 2.65 tall, with 1 cm of foam above and below it; the pocket's open edges are rounded (5 mm radius) and its floor stands 2 mm proud until pressed (about 1.25 N once on the frame). Two are already pushed fully onto the frame's right-hand corners (y -20). The other two lie flat on the table (they are the same either way up) beside the bare left-hand corners, pocket facing their corner: the back of the pocket at the corner's x and at y +30.
scoring: Judged at the end with a tape measure. A bare corner counts when a protector is fully on it and let go: pushed fully home both ways: each closed wall's outer face 2.5 cm past the frame's edge, within 4 mm (the corner is then at the back of the pocket); the pocket's floor under the frame's front and its roof over the frame's back, the foam squeezed onto the frame (no gap a 1 mm feeler gauge, slid in at the pocket's open mouth, passes between the frame's front and the pocket floor); the protector square and level with the frame within 6 degrees; no part of either gripper within 1.5 cm of the protector. 0 if a right-hand protector was pulled off or moved more than 5 mm along either edge, or if the frame was ever dropped (tilted over 15 degrees, or slid 1.5 cm down off a block) or doesn't end flat on both blocks (within 3 degrees). Otherwise 0.5 for each bare corner that counts, except that with both counting it is 1.0 once the frame and both protectors are still (no visible movement for 1 s; in the sim each moves under 1 cm/s and turns under 0.5 rad/s), else 0.75. The trial ends at the run limit, or when 1.0 has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull the two fitted left-hand protectors off and lay them back on their marks, pockets facing their corners; leave the right-hand two on; put the frame back centred on the blocks. Nothing is used up.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz control). The foam's squeeze is a sprung rigid floor in each loose pocket (2,500 N/m, 2 mm proud: about 1.25 N once on); the rest of the foam is rigid, and rounded lips on the pocket's open edges stand in for foam giving at the opening. The frame is one rigid body: moulding, one slab for the glass, mount and back, and the two fitted protectors. Foam friction 0.3, frame 0.6.
